goal_summary: Bounded source investigation and primary-literature curation of the five IMA-approved single-reference critical-element mineral species from Round 129's preserved frontier queue with open-access type descriptions in European Journal of Mineralogy (volumes 36 and 38): spaltiite (IMA:2014-012, Tl2Cu2As2S5), tianhuixinite (IMA:2022-081, (MoO3)3*H2O), zhenruite (IMA:2022-050, (MoO3)2(H2O)), keutschite (IMA:2014-038, Cu2AgAsS4), and heimite (IMA:2022-019, PbCu2(AsO4)(OH)3(H2O)2). Direct inspection of IMA_Master_List_(2026-09).pdf (pages 91, 112, 203, 217, 240) resolved the exact published EJM volume/page citations (correcting the approximate citations carried in Round 129's deferred queue) and identified the next batch of uncurated EJM critical-mineral candidates.

curated_sources_and_records.chemistry_summary: Table 2 (p. 31) JEOL JXA 8530F FE-EPMA WDS chemistry (n = 10 points on main grain in polished section N 9528: mean Cu 15.46(12) wt%, Ag 0.15(6) wt%, As 17.36(14) wt%, Sb 0.41(5) wt%, Tl 47.41(19) wt%, Pb n.d., S 19.20(8) wt%, Total 99.99(32) wt%; Table 2 apfu on 11 atoms: Cu 2.04(1), Ag 0.01(0), As 1.94(1), Sb 0.03(0), Tl 1.95(1), S 5.03(1))
primary_source_discrepancies_documented: The Abstract (p. 27) and Section 5 (p. 30) print the empirical formula on the basis of 11 apfu as Tl1.94Cu2.04Ag0.01As1.95Sb0.03S5.03 and Cu2.04Ag0.01Tl1.94As1.95Sb0.03S5.03, respectively, swapping the Tl = 1.95(1) and As = 1.94(1) apfu coefficients printed in Table 2 (p. 31; where 47.41 wt% Tl / 204.383 = 0.23197 and 17.36 wt% As / 74.9216 = 0.23171 confirm Tl1.95 and As1.94 apfu).
Section 1 (p. 28) and the Figure 3b caption (p. 30) print the mineral symbol as Spti, whereas the Figure 3a caption (p. 30) prints Spli.

Table 4 (p. 33) prints the row label 'R1(F): all, observed' alongside '12.18 %, 14.08 %', transposing the 'all' and 'observed' labels relative to the Abstract (p. 27), which confirms R1 = 12.18 % for the 4753 observed reflections with Fo > 4sigma(Fo).
Section 3 (p. 30) prints the Vickers micro-indentation hardness units as 'kg mm2' ('with a mean of 47 kg mm2') instead of 'kg mm-2' (printed in the Abstract on p. 27).

The Abstract (p. 27) lists the eight strongest powder X-ray diffraction lines using dcalc and Icalc values from Table 3 (p. 32) while printing intensity 40 instead of 100 for 021 and omitting minus signs on hkl.

curated_sources_and_records.chemistry_summary: Table 1 (p. 41) Shimadzu EPMA-1720 WDS chemistry (n = 8 spots: mean MoO3 96.81 wt% [SD 2.4 wt%], H2O* = 4.04 wt% added in ideal stoichiometric ratio to measured MoO3, Total 100.85 wt%, empirical formula (Mo1.00O3)3*H2O on the basis of 10 O apfu)
primary_source_discrepancies_documented: The Abstract (p. 39) and Section 2.2 (p. 41) report Dcalc = 4.131 g/cm3 (calculated from the empirical formula and powder XRD unit-cell volume V = 361.74(2) A3), whereas Table 3 (p. 47) reports rho_cal = 4.11 g/cm3 from the single-crystal XRD unit-cell volume V = 361.88(9) A3 with Z = 2.

Table 1 (p. 41) reports H2O* = 4.04 wt% with footnote '* Added in ideal value' (giving Total = 100.85 wt% with MoO3 = 96.81 wt%), whereas Section 2.2 (p. 42) states that ideal (MoO3)3*H2O requires MoO3 96.00 wt% and H2O 4.00 wt% (4.04 wt% is the stoichiometric H2O scaled to the measured 96.81 wt% MoO3).
Section 1 (p. 40) prints the RRUFF deposition number as 220024, whereas the Figure 2 caption (p. 41) prints R220024.

curated_sources_and_records.chemistry_summary: Table 1 (p. 41) Shimadzu EPMA-1720 WDS chemistry (n = 7 spots: mean MoO3 93.24 wt% [SD 1.81 wt%], ideal H2O* = 5.89 wt%, Total 99.13 wt%, empirical formula (Mo1.00O3)2*H2O on the basis of 7 O apfu)
primary_source_discrepancies_documented: The September 2026 IMA Master List (PDF p. 240) formats the ideal formula as (MoO3)2(H2O), whereas Gu et al. (2026) write (MoO3)2*H2O.

Table 3 (p. 47) prints Z = 2 for natural zhenruite ((MoO3)2*H2O, V = 248.89(2) A3) alongside Z = 4 under the same header '(MoO3)2*H2O' for synthetic zhenruite from Benard et al. (1994, V = 248.4 A3), where Z = 4 corresponds to the hemihydrate formula unit MoO3*1/2H2O rather than (MoO3)2*H2O.

curated_sources_and_records.chemistry_summary: Table 2 (p. 4) JEOL JXA 8530F FE-EPMA WDS chemistry (n = 5 spots on one grain: mean Ag 23.46 wt% [SD 0.34], Cu 29.53 wt% [SD 0.18], Mn 0.031 wt% [SD 0.01], As 16.09 wt% [SD 0.67], Sb 1.20 wt% [SD 0.84], Pb 0.11 wt% [SD 0.07], S 29.06 wt% [SD 0.15], mean of spot totals 99.46 wt% [SD 0.50; sum of rounded means 99.481 wt%]; Table 2 empirical formulas on 8 apfu, 4 S apfu, and 4 Me apfu)
primary_source_discrepancies_documented: The Abstract (p. 1) reports the axial ratio for a = 5.5834(15), c = 10.021(3) A as 'a : b : c = 1 : 1 : 0.897', which equals c/(2a) = 0.8974 rather than c/a = 1.7948.

Both the Abstract (p. 1) and Section 3 (p. 3) print the empirical formula 'calculated on the basis of eight atoms' as Cu2.05Ag0.96(As0.95Sb0.04)Sigma0.99S4.00, whereas Table 2 (p. 4) reports Cu2.00Ag0.97(As0.95Sb0.04)Sigma1.99S4.03 on 8 apfu (4Me + 4S), Cu1.99Ag0.96(As0.95Sb0.04)Sigma1.99S4.00 on 4 S apfu, and Cu2.02Ag0.97(As0.96Sb0.04)Sigma2.00S4.05 on 4 Me apfu.

Table 2 (p. 4) footnote prints the (As + Sb) site sums as (As0.95Sb0.04)Sigma1.99 (for both 8 apfu and 4 S apfu) and (As0.96Sb0.04)Sigma2.00 (for 4 Me apfu), printing Sigma1.99 instead of Sigma0.99 and Sigma2.00 instead of Sigma1.00.

Section 3 (p. 3) prints a comma decimal separator in the ideal Ag weight percentage ('29.01 Cu, 24,62 Ag, 17.10 As, and 29.28 S, for a total of 100.00', where the four rounded values sum to 100.01 wt%).
Section 4 (p. 3) prints the MoKalpha X-ray wavelength as 'lambda = 0.7173 A', omitting the zero present in 'lambda = 0.71073 A' on p. 4 and in Table 3.

curated_sources_and_records.chemistry_summary: Table 1 (p. 155) Cameca SX100 WDS EPMA chemistry (n = 11 spots: mean CuO 28.64 wt% [SD 1.05], PbO 39.89 wt% [SD 0.93], CaO 0.25 wt% [SD 0.26], As2O5 21.73 wt% [SD 0.72], H2O_calc* 9.49 wt% by difference to 100.00 wt%; empirical formula Pb1.04Ca0.03Cu2.10As1.10H6.14O9 on 9 O apfu, or Pb0.97Ca0.02Cu1.95As1.02H7O9 with H2O_calc = 11.64 wt% and Total = 102.15 wt% for 7 H apfu)
primary_source_discrepancies_documented: The September 2026 IMA Master List (PDF p. 91) formats the ideal formula as PbCu2(AsO4)(OH)3(H2O)2, whereas Malcherek et al. (2024) write PbCu2(AsO4)(OH)3*2H2O (and PbCu2(AsO4)(OH)3*2(H2O) in Section 4, p. 155, and Table 2, p. 157).
The Abstract (p. 153) reports the unit-cell volume uncertainty as V = 780.33(8) A3, whereas Table 2 (p. 157) reports V = 780.33(11) A3 for both the monoclinic P21/n and orthorhombic Pnma refinements.

The Abstract (p. 153) prints the empirical formula on the basis of 9 O apfu as Pb1.04Ca0.03Cu2.10As1.10H6.14O9, whereas Section 4 (p. 155) omits the trailing zeroes on Cu and As (Pb1.04Ca0.03Cu2.1As1.1H6.14O9) and also gives Pb0.97Ca0.02Cu1.95As1.02H7O9 when H is fixed at 7 apfu.
